subject: MSA/SOW: clarification on SLA exceptions, uptime & latency draft clauses
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <procurements@medwell.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@medwell.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: specific language for uptime/latency exceptions (MSA/SOW + order form)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. Procurement and legal reviewed the draft MSA and want tighter language for the SLA addendum. Two asks from our side:

1) We need concrete exception language for both uptime and latency events (examples: regional infra outage, maintenance windows, and third-party CDN failure). Please indicate what qualifies as an "exception" versus a breach, and the process for credit calculation.

2) We need order-form-friendly wording we can attach to purchase orders so our finance team can sign off quickly — ideally a short clause we can paste into our PO and SOW.

Attached: MedWell_Requested_SLA_Clauses_v1.docx (docx), MSA_SOW_Redlines.pdf (pdf).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited exception for on-prem connectors during synchronization windows and provide suggested wording for latency SLOs (p95 / p99 thresholds)? Our target is to close legal review by end of next week.

Thanks,

Alyssa Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
MedWell Health
[attachment: MedWell_Requested_SLA_Clauses_v1.docx (docx)]
[attachment: MSA_SOW_Redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <procurements@medwell.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: specific language for uptime/latency exceptions (MSA/SOW + order form)

Alyssa — thanks for the clear asks and the redlines. Copying Karthik (sales lead) and Laura (legal ops) to propose final wording.

Quick summary of our approach:
- We can provide two deliverables: (A) a concise order-form clause that goes into the PO/SOW and (B) a full SLA addendum suitable to attach to the MSA that enumerates exceptions, credit methodology, and escalation paths.
- We treat scheduled maintenance and declared regional provider outages as "exceptions" (no credit), while unplanned service availability below the agreed uptime for >X minutes qualifies for credit. We'll propose concrete thresholds.

Initial proposed order-form clause (one-liner suggestion you can paste into a PO):
"Redwood Inference will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.95% monthly uptime for hosted inference endpoints. For the avoidance of doubt, downtime caused by Customer-managed on-prem connectors, scheduled maintenance (48 hours notice), and third-party provider outages are not covered by this SLA. Credits for qualifying availability breaches will be calculated as a percentage of the affected monthly service fees and applied at the next billing cycle."

Questions for you:
- Do you need separate latency SLOs per route (inference vs embeddings) or a single site-wide latency SLO?
- Is MedWell comfortable with p95/p99 as the reporting metrics for latency?

Next steps: Laura will draft the formal addendum language and Karthik will collate order-form wording and credit bands. If that timeline works we'll aim to send a consolidated draft by Monday EOD.

Soojin Lee
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[linked: HS-1234567]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <procurements@medwell.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: specific language for uptime/latency exceptions (MSA/SOW + order form)

Alyssa — looping in the order-form draft and proposed credit bands. Thanks for the patience.

Key points I recommend including in the order form (draft attached: orderform_sla_clauses_v2.docx):
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly for hosted API endpoints. Credit tiers: 99.0-99.95% = 10% of monthly fees for affected service; 95.0-99.0% = 25%; <95% = 50%.
- Latency: p95 under normal load <= 220ms; p99 <= 600ms (these are measured at Redwood edge for requests routed to hosted instances).
- Exceptions: provider regional outages, scheduled maintenance (we will give 48 hours notice unless emergency), and customer-managed on-prem connector sync windows. The order form should include a simple definition of "Customer-managed connector."
- Exception handling process: Customer opens a support ticket with the incident window; Redwood will validate and publish an incident summary. Credit requests must be submitted within 30 days of the incident end.

One proposed wording snippet for the order form (concise):
"Redwood Inference SLA Addendum: Redwood will target 99.95% monthly availability for hosted inference endpoints and will publish monthly availability reports. Availability credits for qualifying outages will be applied per the credit tiers attached. Exclusions include scheduled maintenance, third-party provider outages, and Customer-managed connector sync windows. Latency SLOs (p95/p99) apply at the Redwood edge; on-prem performance is subject to Customer-managed network conditions."

I've attached orderform_sla_clauses_v2.docx with editable bullets and credit tables. Laura — can you add the final legal-safe phrasing for the credit submission window and the maximum cumulative credit cap?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[attachment: orderform_sla_clauses_v2.docx (docx)]

From: Alyssa Turner <procurements@medwell.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir.shah@medwell.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: specific language for uptime/latency exceptions (MSA/SOW + order form)

Karthik & Soojin — this is helpful, appreciate the speed. A few quick items from Legal/Procurement after reviewing your drafts:

- Latency SLOs: we need p95 and p99 for both "generation" and "embedding" routes separately. Can you split the measurement buckets?
- On-prem connector exception: MedWell will not accept a blanket exclusion for all on-prem connectors. We can accept an exclusion limited to scheduled sync windows that are >30 minutes and pre-declared. Can you add language that requires customers to declare sync windows in writing 72 hours in advance for the exclusion to apply?
- Credit cap: MedWell requests a cumulative monthly credit cap of 100% of monthly fees for severe failures; your draft didn't specify a cap. Please propose one.

If you can incorporate the changes and send a redline PDF, we can get legal to sign off quickly. We will also need the final order form clause by Tuesday so finance can process the PO.

DocuSign will be used for the signature: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?s=ABCDEF123456

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
MedWell Health
